title: Where the honey comes from.
intro: Our hives sit in Manalapan Township, New Jersey. The bees forage the wildflowers around them, and everything in a Bogabee jar comes from those hives.

sections.heading: The bees
sections.body: Honey bees do almost all the work here. Each colony raises its own young, builds its own wax comb, and stores more honey than it needs for winter. The extra is what goes in the jar.

sections.heading: What they forage
sections.body: A honey bee can fly a few miles from the hive for nectar. Ours visit the wildflowers, gardens and fields around Manalapan, which is why the honey is called wildflower: its color and taste follow whatever is in bloom.

sections.heading: How it gets to the jar
sections.body: We take frames the bees have finished and capped with wax, spin the honey out, and pour it into jars by hand in small batches. It is never filtered, so the natural pollen and enzymes stay in.

seasons.name: Spring
seasons.text: Colonies grow fast as the first blooms open.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.text: The main nectar flow. Honey supers go on and fill up.

seasons.name: Late summer
seasons.text: Harvest. Capped frames come off and get jarred.

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.text: The bees cluster to stay warm and live on the honey they kept.

keeper: Danny keeps the Bogabee hives. Follow along on Instagram for the hives, the harvests and the occasional sunflower.
